title: Error Chronicle: Temporal Fault Map & Payload Snapshot UI
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design a compact, temporal-first diagnostics surface called Error Chronicle that helps engineers trace a failed request series across time. The UI combines a horizontal 'temporal fault map' (showing attempts, retries, fallbacks, and downstream calls) with a right-column payload snapshot panel that surfaces request/response headers, truncated token diffs, and model variant switches. The goal is to reduce mean time to root cause by making retry patterns, transient vs deterministic failures, and payload differences immediately visible. This ticket covers interaction patterns, visual language, accessibility, prototype flows for 0, 1, and multiple retries, and handoff assets for engineering (React + Canvas).
acceptance_criteria: Temporal fault map visualizes up to 50 sequential attempts with clear status markers for success, transient-failure, permanent-failure, and fallback
Hovering an attempt shows a compact diff of input token prefixes and model variant at that attempt
Payload snapshot panel shows request metadata (route, model, seq length), request body, response body, and server-side error code with copy-to-clipboard for full payload
UX flows for canary rollouts: map highlights attempts routed to new model variant and supports toggling to only show canary traffic
Prototype includes a keyboard-accessible timeline scrubber and meets color-contrast/accessibility guidelines
Design handoff includes component specs, responsive behavior for narrow consoles, and a list of required telemetry fields for engineering
discussion: 2025-02-11 Maya Patel: Kickoff — scoped to Console Diagnostics project. Proposed 3-pane layout: timeline, state legend, payload snapshot. Need PM priorities for canary support.
2025-02-18 Liam O'Connor: First wireframes attached. Raised trade-off: full token diffs are heavy; propose truncation + expand-to-full via modal (engineering asked for telemetry keys).
2025-02-22 Jemma Alvarez (PM): Prioritized highlighting canary vs stable routing and adding toggle to filter only failed attempts. Added PM-233 as dependency.

2025-02-26 Design review: Engineering asked to avoid heavy DOM for 50-entry timelines. Decided to render timeline with Canvas and virtualized list. Update: include visual affordance for automatic fallbacks.
2025-03-03 Accessibility pass: color updates for contrast. Need keyboard scrubber prototype before sign-off. Liam will ship updated prototype by 2025-03-05.
notes: Avoid replicating existing Debug Trace patterns; Chronicle must emphasize temporal causality (what happened when) and make retries and model variant routing first-class. Keep the default collapsed state lightweight for consoles with dense traffic; expand on demand. Consider eventual integration with Request Insights for correlated traces.
design_rationale: Users frequently lose time switching between a flat list of failed requests and payload tabs. By surfacing a time-ordered map and inline payload diffs, engineers can quickly separate infrastructure flakiness from model regressions. Canvas-based timeline ensures performance while the payload snapshot provides quick context without navigating away.
open_questions: Should the timeline aggregate low-volume retries into a collapsed cluster by default?
What is the maximum permitted payload size to render inline before forcing modal download?
Do we annotate inferred error taxonomy (transient vs deterministic) on the timeline or only in the details panel?
